takeaway: Unfractionated heparin is a tangle of chains of varying size; LMWH contains only short chains and reduces DVT extension and recurrence by 38%.

question.text: Comparing LMWH with unfractionated heparin, which one of the following statements is correct?

answer.text: LMWH reduces the risk of extension or recurrence of DVT by 38% compared with unfractionated heparin.
answer.say: LMWH reduces the risk of extension or recurrence of DVT by thirty-eight percent compared with unfractionated heparin.

lines.text: Here is heparin, side by side with its low molecular weight cousin.
Unfractionated heparin is a tangle of polymers of varying molecular weights.
It needs regular APTT monitoring, not a once-daily infusion.
LMWH is fractionated, cut down to short chains only.
lines.say: (laugh) LMWH is fractionated, cut down to short chains only.

lines.text: That is why it is used for DVT prophylaxis in surgery.
It is also better at stopping a DVT from extending or coming back, by thirty-eight percent.
And it carries a lower risk of heparin-induced thrombocytopenia.
